subtitle: Netflix acquiring Warner Brothers, shook me personally...
title: Is Netflix Bullish or Bearish?
description: Netflix acquiring Warner Brothers, shook me personally...
body_html:
Netflix acquiring Warner Brothers was just another nail in the coffin for me ⚰️.

I will talk briefly about the Netflix stock at the end, but this is a bit of a personal journey piece. If you do not want to read my physical media rant, skip down to where you see the chart emojis for the Netflix stock discussion 📈📉📈📉📈📉📈📉

A few months ago, I was in the mood to watch Jurassic Park, and have my daughters, who are 6 and 7, watch it for the first time. This ended up becoming a very costly decision…

I logged onto Amazon prime, looked up Jurassic Park, and was slightly agitated that I had to pay for a movie that came out in 1993. You are already paying ~$20 a month for Amazon Prime…then another $3.79 to rent a move that came out 32 years ago…and still have ads! If you are a young Gen Z, or Gen Alpha, this is NOT how streaming services used to be. You paid a small monthly fee and got everything. Period.

Subscribe now

The decision to watch Jurassic Park became costly because my daughter unexpectedly became obsessed with Dinosaurs…which turned into a trip to Universal Studios. My youngest loves E.T., and you can see below her swag as well. The park tickets were over $1k and the fast passes alone for 4 days for 4 people was over $4k alone. Probably another $700 in junk. We had a great time, but it certainly made me reflect on showing my daughter that Jurassic Park movie 😂!

But I am not here to complain about the over priced theme parks, with entry prices climbing as quickly as cocaine (literally). More so the streaming services. No, $3.79 isn’t much…but its the morality of charging for a movie that is 3 decades old. The morality of streaming services splitting up series amongst platforms, forcing you to have multiple subscriptions. The fact that they retain the rights to edit or alter a movie or show’s script, which was not the original Director’s artwork. The fact that we are getting nickeled and dimed 🪙 over everything is the issue! Especially for old movies!

And hence, I started my physical media journey. And to be clear, I am a rookie compared to some of the physical media collectors I have watched on TikTok. But am sitting at 543 movies, and multiple TV series so far. But back to the story…

I had a few old DVD’s in the basement stored away in a box. About 10 or so, nothing crazy. Spiderman and a few of the Star Wars movies. Knew that I wanted more though. But you don’t just make a collection magically appear. For simplicity say there are 100 movies you like, each with 2-5 parts or sequels to them, that would be about 500 movies. We will use the Spider-Man movie collection as an example. If you want all of them, new, you are looking at between $45 to $69. And again, you have 100’s of movies and series that you like. By going with new, your movie collection can cost upwards of $10,000 to $20,000 very easily…and you may want more!

Yes, I could go buy it all new, but I have always loved thrift stores; maybe its the musty smell when you walk in, or the incredibly…interesting 😳…people browsing around. Heck, you can people watch alone and its a fun trip in itself lol. Maybe I love them because I grew up incredibly poor, and it’s a “normal” place for me mentally, a childhood imprint. Worn out Goodwill shoes were my normal Christmas gift as a kid; this is one of the reasons I became a stock investor. But as I was walking around a thrift store I noticed that the DVD section had several of my favorite movies from when I was younger. “Cast Away” was one of my favorites, a movie about a FedEx delivery man surviving on an island after a plane crash. And not far from that DVD was the entire Matrix series…who isn’t a Keanu Reeves fan?! I looked at the side of the cabinet and it read: “10 for $1”. What a deal! I picked up my first haul of about 30ish DVD’s that day. The entire Matrix series cost me about 10 cents. If I bought it new, it would have been about $20 to $60, depending on format type. I bought the dip 😂!

So far, I have spent about $600 for my collection in total. And I will have it forever, no more $3.79 charges, with ads and as the the director intended. What I try to do is complete series just by thrifting. For example, I thrifted 4 of the 5 Underworld movies, but could not find #1; so I went to Vintage Stock (a used physical media store) to complete the collection. It cost me about $7 to complete the series on my own. I love thrifting DVD’s because it always feels like a treasure hunt, you never know what you are going to find and as you can tell, is pretty inexpensive. You can be rich or poor and do this.

One side note benefit of thrifting DVD’s, aside from having the film forever: so many just go into landfills. Im not the “greenest” type of person…but it feels good knowing I’m saving the earth a little bit of plastic lol. Also some people will say DVD’s take up space. There are so many storage methodologies out there. I built my own modern shelving, customized to the room, on the wall. It takes up 0% floor space. Heck, you could put thousands in a binder.

The next step for me is to create my own streaming service that way my family and I can watch any of these DVDs from anywhere at anytime on any device. Maybe this will be an update in a few months. Ive seen it done, but not sure on how to do it, yet.

The reason I am giving you this long winded story, is it ties directly into Netflix acquiring Warner Brothers.

📈📉📈📉📈📉📈📉📈📉📈📉📈📉📈📉📈📉📈📉📈📉📈📉📈📉📈📉📈📉

Netflix is a company I covered back in October: Bearish on Netflix; the stock is down -11% since that video.

Full disclosure, I closed my short position, in profit, due to going on vacation and due to the stock split; many subscribers are still shorting NFLX. Regardless the quick point is, the acquisition is actually, at least short term, bearish, especially since the acquisition was so costly at $82.7 Billion. Normally acquisitions of this size spook investors, because they are uncertain on how the company will perform with the new company. Can Netflix turn a profit, or build a vast revenue stream, of more than $82B? Will customers like it? How long will it last if successful? Can Netflix keep Warner Brother’s famous titles, like Harry Potter or Lord of the Rings, alive? So many questions and unknowns will scare big money off, oftentimes in the short term. Only time will tell if Netflix will be successful or not, and large investors are unlikely to gamble on that in the interim, when more promising companies are present.

Subscribe now

Look below, at the note in acquisition letter, Netflix states: “…expects to attract and retain more members.” and “expects to realize at least $2-3 billion of cost savings.”1 There are no promises or guarantees.

Stock splits are normally short term bearish, long term bullish for companies. Aside from vacation, it was another reason I cut my short position. But an acquisition of this size, $82B, when Netflix only brings in about $6.9B annually (and that was a record year) is going to spook the big money, at least for now. There are many examples of spooking investors, AT&T comes to mind, when they acquired Time Warner for a similar $85B.

The main point: Nothing about Netflix is bullish.

  • Price action trending down, below the 200 day. This is a hard rule. I NEVER buy stocks below their 200 day moving average. Ever. Sure, maybe it has a bounce…we can talk again then. I want a trend, not a bounce.

  • We do not know if Netflix will be successful with Warner Brother’s media line. I already see concerns on social media about Netflix just pumping out crap content, where WB was more original (matter of opinion here).

  • Don’t get me wrong…I don’t think Netflix is going anywhere, and long long term, It will be fine. But I personally speculate it has another year or two of painful price action.

I talked about the DVD’s as well, simply because we do not know what will stay, change, or go with WB or even HBO. What movies will Netflix NOT include on their streaming platforms? We simply do not have those answers. Physical media collectors will care not. It honestly just felt like a good time to talk about a new passion of mine 😅.

In summary:

  • Netflix is still bearish.

  • Consider picking up your favorite movies and shows, so you can have them forever, and not be nickeled and dimed to death for the rest of your life.

Hope you have a great weekend and I will see you bright and early tomorrow morning. There are many stocks quickly approaching buy zones!
